AO_8BAD1B_BOOTSTRAP.summary: Bootstrap/lock marker table of the shared storage layer. Normally holds exactly one row, created lazily, with C_IS_LOCKED false or NULL (both read as unlocked), the first time the storage layer is touched or the lock flag is read; it is never deleted. Its only meaningful content is the global 'storage locked' flag, raised while a backup restore or data migration rewrites the plugin tables so that all cluster nodes refuse ordinary writes. If several rows exist, the flag is considered raised when ANY row has it true, and lock/unlock writes the flag to every row.

columns.ID: Auto-increment surrogate key; no meaning (normally 1).
columns.C_IS_LOCKED: Boolean storage-lock flag. true = the plugin data is exclusively locked by a running restore/migration (other operations must fail or wait); false or NULL = unlocked. Set to true when the lock is taken and back to false when released (also on forced unlock). A row stuck at true after a crash blocks writes until it is reset.

AO_8BAD1B_ITEM_TYPE.summary: Registry that maps item type keys (strings) to compact integer ids used by other tables. One row per distinct item type key ever used; C_KEY is unique. Rows are created on demand (insert-if-absent, retried on unique-constraint conflict) the first time a type key needs an id, and are never updated or deleted, so an id stays stable forever. Referenced by AO_8BAD1B_ROW.C_ITEM_TYPE and AO_8BAD1B_ITEM_EVENTS_V2.C_TYPEID (and other item-referencing tables).

columns.ID: Auto-increment integer item type id. This number is what other tables store as the item type; it is local to this database (not portable between instances; backups store the key string instead).
columns.C_KEY: Item type key, non-blank, unique, max 190 chars. Item type keys are module complete keys of the form '<plugin key>:<module key>'; the built-in ones all start with 'com.almworks.jira.structure:type-' (e.g. 'com.almworks.jira.structure:type-issue', '...:type-folder', '...:type-generator', '...:type-effector', '...:type-memo', '...:type-project', '...:type-user', '...:type-label', '...:type-status', '...:type-version', '...:type-sprint'); third-party item types use their own plugin key.

AO_8BAD1B_ITEM_EVENTS_V2.summary: Cluster-wide journal of 'item changed' notifications, used only on Jira Data Center (a single-node server keeps this journal in memory and leaves the table empty). Each row says that one item (issue, folder, generator, user, ...) changed at a given time, so other nodes can invalidate caches and refresh structures. Event ids are allocated from a per-node id partition recorded in AO_8BAD1B_NODE_SIGNS_V2: a node writes consecutive ids C_MINEID, C_MINEID+1, ... below C_MAXEID. Rows are only inserted, never updated. Rows in a node's partition are bulk-deleted whenever that node (re)initialises its partition (node start, partition overflow, or write failure) and the whole table is emptied by the maintenance option 'cleanupItemTracker'. Other nodes read the events of each live node in id order starting after the last id they have seen.

columns.C_ID: Event id (bigint), explicitly assigned, not auto-increment. Lies in the half-open range [C_MINEID, C_MAXEID) of the writing node's row in AO_8BAD1B_NODE_SIGNS_V2; consecutive within that node's partition in write order.
columns.C_TIMESTAMP: Time the change was recorded, epoch milliseconds (server clock of the writing node).
columns.C_TYPEID: Item type of the changed item: an AO_8BAD1B_ITEM_TYPE.ID.
columns.C_ITEMID: Numeric item id for items identified by a long id (e.g. Jira issue id for '...:type-issue', folder id, generator id, project id). Written as 0 for items identified by a string id. Exactly one of C_ITEMID (non-zero) / C_ITEMSID (non-null, non-blank) identifies the item.
columns.C_ITEMSID: String item id for items identified by a string (e.g. user key for '...:type-user', label text for '...:type-label', status/priority/issue type id for those types); max 190 chars. NULL for long-id items.

AO_8BAD1B_NODE_SIGNS_V2.summary: One row per Jira Data Center node that has ever written item events: the node's event-id partition and its current runtime signature. Unique by C_NODE. A row is created the first time a node initialises its event journal; afterwards each re-initialisation (node start, overflow, failure recovery) rewrites C_SIGN and C_UPDATED in place and deletes all events of the partition, then restarts numbering at C_MINEID. New nodes get the next partition: C_MINEID = max(C_MAXEID over all rows, starting id) and C_MAXEID = C_MINEID + partition size. Defaults: partition size 1,000,000 and first partition starting at 1,000,000 (both overridable by the dark-feature/system properties 'structure.cluster.event.range' and 'structure.cluster.event.initial'). Rows of dead nodes are ignored by readers but not deleted (except by the maintenance item tracker cleanup, which deletes all rows together with all events). Changes to this table are serialised by the cluster lock 'com.almworks.structure..ievent-signature-lock.0'. A reader that sees another live node's signature change resets its change tracking.

columns.ID: Auto-increment surrogate key; no meaning.
columns.C_NODE: Jira cluster node id (as reported by Jira's cluster manager), max 190 chars, unique. The literal '-' is used when the instance is not clustered.
columns.C_MINEID: First event id (inclusive) of this node's partition in AO_8BAD1B_ITEM_EVENTS_V2.C_ID.
columns.C_MAXEID: End of this node's partition (exclusive): the node never writes event ids >= this value. Fixed when the row is created.
columns.C_SIGN: Runtime signature: an arbitrary non-zero 32-bit signed integer generated randomly (time/nanotime based) each time the node re-initialises its partition. A change of this value tells other nodes that the partition was wiped and restarted. 0 is never stored as a valid signature.
columns.C_UPDATED: Time of the last (re)initialisation of this row, epoch milliseconds.

AO_8BAD1B_ROW.summary: Persistent forest rows. Each row of a stored structure forest refers to one row record here, which binds a row id to an item (item type + id) and a semantics code. Row records are immutable: they are created when an item is added to a stored forest (or when a backup is restored with its original row ids) and are never updated or deleted by normal operation, even when the forest no longer uses them (one item may have many row records). Public row id mapping: the row id used everywhere else (forests in AO_8BAD1B_FOREST/AO_8BAD1B_FOREST_CHANGE, history, REST, backups, API) is ID * 2 (always even and positive). Odd positive row ids are transient rows produced by generators and never stored here; negative row ids are temporary. To find the record of public row id r, read ID = r / 2. A restore inserts records with explicit ID = r / 2.

columns.ID: Auto-increment integer key. Public row id = ID * 2 (e.g. ID 7 is row 14). Overflow (ID <= 0) is an error.
columns.C_ITEM_TYPE: Item type of the row's item: AO_8BAD1B_ITEM_TYPE.ID.
columns.C_ITEM_STRING_ID: String id of the item when the item type uses string ids (user key, label, status id, priority id, issue type id, resolution id, group name, canonical version name, '/<text>' text folders, ...); max 190 chars. NULL for long-id items.
columns.C_ITEM_LONG_ID: Numeric id of the item for long-id types: Jira issue id for '...:type-issue', AO_8BAD1B_FOLDER.ID for '...:type-folder', public generator id (AO_8BAD1B_GENERATOR.C_ID * 2) for '...:type-generator', effector id for '...:type-effector', memo/note id, project id, version id, sprint id, etc. Written as 0 (not NULL) for string-id items.
columns.C_SEMANTICS: Row semantics code (signed 64-bit) carried with the row and exposed through the public row API. For rows created by users or by synchronisers in a stored structure it is 0; when a row is copied (e.g. restore or migration) the source row's value is kept. Value -1 denotes the virtual super-root and is never stored. Other values are opaque to storage and must be preserved.

AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE.summary: One row per structure (the named, permission-controlled container of a forest). Created when a user/API creates or copies a structure, or by restore with an explicit ID. Updated in place when name, description, owner, archived flag or permissions change. Deleted when the structure is deleted, together with its AO_8BAD1B_FOREST row, all its AO_8BAD1B_FOREST_CHANGE rows, its history and its issue index entries. ID is the public structure id used by every other table (C_STRUCTURE_ID, C_OWNING_STRUCTURE columns) and in the API/REST.

columns.ID: Auto-increment structure id (public, positive). Explicit values are inserted on restore.
columns.C_NAME: Structure name as shown to users, required, max 190 chars.
columns.C_DESCRIPTION: Free-text description (unlimited text). NULL when empty.
columns.C_OWNER: Jira user key (not user name) of the owner; NULL when there is no owner (empty owner is stored as NULL).
columns.C_ARCHIVED: Boolean: true = archived (hidden from normal lists, read-only to most operations); false/NULL = active.
columns.C_PERMISSONS: (Column name is misspelt in the schema; keep it.) Structure permission rules as a JSON object, or NULL when there are no rules and edit-inheritance is off. Keys: "permissions" (array of rules, omitted when empty) and "editInheritance" (true, omitted when false). Each rule is either {"type":"set","subject":<subject>,"level":<level>} or {"type":"apply","structure":<structure id>} (apply the rules of another structure). Subject is {"type":"anyone"}, {"type":"user","name":"<user key>"}, {"type":"group","name":"<group name>"} or {"type":"project.role","project":<project id>,"role":<project role id>}. Level is one of the strings "NONE", "VIEW", "EDIT", "EDIT_GENERATORS", "ADMIN": in this column the automation level is always written as "EDIT_GENERATORS" (legacy name of the 'automate' level) and "EDIT_GENERATORS" is read back as automate. Rules are evaluated in order, later rules override earlier ones. "editInheritance": true means editing the structure additionally requires edit permission on the parent issue ("edit requires parent issue permission"). Example: {"permissions":[{"type":"set","subject":{"type":"group","name":"jira-users"},"level":"VIEW"},{"type":"set","subject":{"type":"project.role","project":10000,"role":10002},"level":"EDIT_GENERATORS"},{"type":"apply","structure":12}],"editInheritance":true}. Unknown keys are ignored on read.

AO_8BAD1B_FOREST.summary: Current forest (tree of rows) of each structure, one row per structure (primary key = structure id). Created with an empty forest and version 0 when the structure is created (or by restore). Every successful forest update rewrites C_FOREST and advances C_VERSION with an optimistic compare-and-set (update ... where structure id = ? and version = old version); a concurrent writer retries. Deleted with the structure. The incremental changes between versions are journaled in AO_8BAD1B_FOREST_CHANGE.

columns.C_STRUCTURE_ID: Structure id (AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE.ID), primary key, not auto-generated.
columns.C_FOREST: Forest JSON: {"rows":[r1,r2,...],"depths":[d1,d2,...]} - two equal-length arrays in depth-first (pre-order) display order: rows are public row ids (even = AO_8BAD1B_ROW.ID*2), depths are 0-based nesting levels (0 = top level; each depth is at most previous depth + 1; first depth is 0). Keys appear in the order rows, depths. An empty forest is {"rows":[],"depths":[]}. On read, a scalar in place of an array is accepted as a one-element array and null elements as 0. Example: {"rows":[14,16,18,20],"depths":[0,1,1,0]} is row 14 with children 16 and 18, followed by top-level row 20.
columns.C_VERSION: Forest version number (int), 0 for a newly created structure. Each update increases it by the number of elementary changes written to AO_8BAD1B_FOREST_CHANGE in that update (so version N means N elementary changes since creation, modulo restore). After a restore the version is set to the value recorded in the backup.

AO_8BAD1B_FOREST_CHANGE.summary: Journal of elementary forest changes per structure, used by clients and other nodes to update a cached forest incrementally from version V to a later one. One row per elementary change. Rows are inserted in the same operation that bumps AO_8BAD1B_FOREST.C_VERSION: if the forest goes from version v to v+k, k rows are written with versions v+1..v+k, in order. Rows are never updated. Old rows are purged: a scheduled job (job key 'forestChanges.lastCleanTime', default every 12 hours) keeps only the latest 501 changes per structure: it deletes the versions below the highest minus 500, so one more than the limit of 500 remains (both numbers are tunable via dark-feature settings); all rows of a structure are deleted with the structure. A reader needing versions older than the oldest retained change must reload the whole forest.

columns.C_ID: Composite bigint key = (structure id << 32) | version, where version is the forest version produced by this change (the change transforms version-1 into version). E.g. structure 5, version 3 -> 5*4294967296+3 = 21474836483. Explicitly assigned (not auto-increment). All changes of structure s lie in [s<<32, (s+1)<<32).
columns.C_CHANGE: The change as a JSON object with a type discriminator "action" first and the remaining properties in alphabetical order. Four kinds: add: {"action":"add","addedForest":<forest>,"after":<row id or 0>,"under":<row id or 0>} - inserts a sub-forest (same {"rows","depths"} format as AO_8BAD1B_FOREST.C_FOREST) as children of 'under' (0 = top level) right after sibling 'after' (0 = as first child). move: {"action":"move","after":<row id or 0>,"movedRows":[row ids],"under":<row id or 0>} - moves the listed rows (with their subtrees) to the given position. remove: {"action":"remove","removedRows":[row ids]} - removes the listed rows with their subtrees. reorder: {"action":"reorder","children":[row ids],"under":<row id or 0>} - sets the order of the children of 'under'. Row ids are public row ids. Example: {"action":"add","addedForest":{"rows":[22],"depths":[0]},"after":16,"under":14}.

AO_8BAD1B_GENERATOR.summary: Stored configuration of generators (automation rules: inserters, extenders, groupers, sorters, filters) placed in structures. One row per generator instance. Created when a generator row is added to a structure (or by restore with an explicit id), updated when its parameters change, deleted when the generator is removed/cleaned up. Public generator id = C_ID * 2 (even, positive); that public id is the long item id of the generator's row ('...:type-generator') in AO_8BAD1B_ROW.

columns.C_ID: Auto-increment integer key. Public generator id = C_ID * 2; restore inserts C_ID = public id / 2.
columns.C_MODULE_KEY: Complete key of the generator module, '<plugin key>:<module key>', max 190 chars. Built-in values include 'com.almworks.jira.structure:inserter-jql', ':agile-board', ':inserter-text', ':inserter-substructure', ':inserter-recent-issues', ':extender-subtasks', ':extender-links', ':extender-agile', ':extender-portfolio-children', ':grouper-field', ':grouper-sprint', ':grouper-agile-epic', ':grouper-text', ':grouper-portfolio-parent', ':grouper-tempo-account', ':grouper-version-name', ':grouper-links', ':sorter-attribute', ':sorter-agile-rank', ':sorter-manual', ':filter-by-field', ':filter-jql', ':filter-text', ':filter-attribute', ':filter-number-attribute', ':filter-sjql', ':filter-item', ':filter-inserter-extender-duplicates', ':filter-sprint' (all prefixed with 'com.almworks.jira.structure').
columns.C_PARAMETERS: Generator parameters as a JSON object (map of parameter name to JSON value; nulls omitted); its keys are defined by each generator type. NULL when the parameter map is empty. Example for a JQL inserter: {"jql":"project = ABC","limit":1000}.
columns.C_OWNING_STRUCTURE: Id of the structure (AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE.ID) the generator belongs to; NULL when not bound to a structure. Used for permission checks and cleanup of generators of deleted structures.

AO_8BAD1B_VIEW.summary: Saved views (column configurations shown on top of a structure). One row per view. Created by users, by restore (explicit ID) and once at first start when the default views are created (guarded by the property 'createdDefaultViews' in AO_8BAD1B_PROPERTY). Updated in place by read-merge-write of the JSON. Deleted when a view is deleted (its AO_8BAD1B_VIEW_TO_STRUCTURE rows are deleted at the same time). ID is the public view id.

columns.ID: Auto-increment public view id (positive).
columns.C_DATA: View definition as a JSON object (nulls omitted, unknown keys ignored on read). Keys: "name" (string, required), "description" (string), "owner" (permission subject, normally {"type":"user","name":"<user key>"}), "permissions" (array of permission rules, same rule/subject grammar as AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE.C_PERMISSONS except that levels are written by their plain names "NONE", "VIEW", "EDIT", "ADMIN"), "specification" (object), and possibly "id" (the view id, written only when the view was created with a known id; ignored on read, the row ID wins). "specification" = {"columns":[<column>...],"columnDisplayMode":1|2,"rowDisplayMode":11|12,"pins":[<csid>...]} where columnDisplayMode 1 = auto-fit, 2 = scrollable (default 1); rowDisplayMode 11 = one line, 12 = text wrapping (default 11); "pins" lists the csids of pinned columns. Each column = {"csid":"<column id unique within the view, decimal string>","key":"<column type>","name":"<header, optional>","parameters":{...}} with column type keys such as "main", "field" (parameter "field": Jira field id like "issuekey", "assignee", "timeestimate", optional "aggregate":"sum"), "progress", "icons" (parameter "fields": list of field ids), "formula", etc.; parameters are type-specific. Example: {"name":"Basic View","owner":{"type":"user","name":"JIRAUSER10000"},"permissions":[{"type":"set","subject":{"type":"anyone"},"level":"VIEW"}],"specification":{"columns":[{"csid":"0","key":"field","parameters":{"field":"issuekey"}},{"csid":"1","key":"main","name":"main"}],"columnDisplayMode":1,"rowDisplayMode":11,"pins":[]}}.

AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE_TO_VIEW.summary: Per-structure view settings: which views are associated with a structure, on which pages they appear in the view menu and which is the default. One row per structure that ever had settings, plus the special row with C_STRUCTURE_ID = 0 holding the global default view settings (used for structures without own settings). Created on first save (version 0); each later save rewrites C_VIEW_SETTINGS with an optimistic compare-and-set on C_VERSION and increments it. Clearing the settings stores NULL settings (the row is kept, version still incremented). After each successful save of a structure's settings (not for row 0), the derived index AO_8BAD1B_VIEW_TO_STRUCTURE is rewritten for that structure.

columns.C_STRUCTURE_ID: Structure id (AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE.ID), or 0 for the global default settings. Primary key, not auto-generated.
columns.C_VIEW_SETTINGS: JSON object {"views":[<associated view>...]} (nulls omitted; an object without "views" means 'settings not defined' -> fall back to defaults). Each associated view = {"view":<view id>,"menuPages":[<page>...],"defaultPages":[<page>...]} in that key order; "menuPages" omitted means the view appears on all pages; "defaultPages" lists pages where it is the default view. Page values: "structure" (structure board), "issue" (issue page panel), "project" (project page tab), "gadget" (dashboard gadget); legacy values "structure-with-details" (read as structure+project), "component", "version", "navigator", "greenhopper" may appear in old data. Menu pages are restricted to structure/issue/project/gadget, default pages to structure/issue/project. Order of the array is the menu order. Example: {"views":[{"view":3,"defaultPages":["structure","project"]},{"view":7,"menuPages":["structure"]}]}. NULL = settings removed.
columns.C_VERSION: Optimistic-lock counter, 0 on insert, +1 on every successful update. Also stamped onto the matching AO_8BAD1B_VIEW_TO_STRUCTURE rows.

AO_8BAD1B_VIEW_TO_STRUCTURE.summary: Reverse index view -> structures, derived from AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE_TO_VIEW, used to find which structures a view is associated with. One row per (structure, associated view) pair of a structure's current settings (only positive view ids). On each successful save of a structure's view settings with new version v, rows (structure, view, v) are inserted for every associated view and then all rows of that structure with C_VERSION < v are deleted. All rows of a view are deleted when the view is deleted. Duplicates are tolerated on read (the structure list is de-duplicated).

columns.ID: Auto-increment surrogate key; no meaning.
columns.C_STRUCTURE_ID: Structure id (AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE.ID) whose settings reference the view.
columns.C_VERSION: The AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE_TO_VIEW.C_VERSION of the structure's settings at the time the row was written; rows with older versions are stale and purged.

AO_8BAD1B_PROPERTY.summary: Global key/value store of the plugin (string values). One row per key. Setting an empty or null value deletes the row; otherwise the row is created or its value overwritten. A restore writes every global property found in the backup. Values are plain strings: booleans as 'true'/'false' (anything other than 'true' reads as false), numbers as decimal text, structured values as JSON. Keys written by the plugin: 'createdDefaultViews' (boolean; true once the default views were created at first start, prevents re-creating them); 'generationTimeLimit' (long, seconds; global limit for generator execution time per structure, overridable per structure in structure properties); 'manualAdjustments.enableForNewStructure' (boolean, default false); 'statistics.sendingEnabled' (boolean; consent to send usage statistics, default false); 'welcomeScreen.help' (JSON {"title":"...","content":"<wiki markup>","contactKeys":["<user key>",...]} for the admin-defined help panel; row removed when cleared); 'appSupport.blockedSerials' (space-separated list of license serial numbers); 'appSupport.lastCheckedSerial' (license serial of the plugin last reported to the vendor's app-support check) and 'appSupport.lastCheckedSerial:<product key>' for extension products; 'sjm.<job key>' (epoch milliseconds of the last run of an internal scheduled job; job keys: 'statistics.lastSentTime', 'forestChanges.lastCleanTime', 'maintenance.scheduled.job'; the original's vendor-report and licence-check jobs are not contract (§1.8), and the replacement neither runs them nor writes their rows); 'maintenance.scheduled.enabled' (boolean, default true); 'maintenance.scheduled.time' ('H:M' daily time, e.g. '3:0' or '23:45', default 3:00); 'maintenance.scheduled.crontab.enabled' (boolean, default false); 'maintenance.scheduled.crontab.schedule' (5-field cron expression minute hour day month weekday, default '0 3 * * *'); 'maintenance.scheduled.parameters' and 'maintenance.manual.parameters' (JSON object of string values, keys: backup, backup-saveHistory, removeOldBackups, removeOldBackups-minFilesToKeep (default 5), removeOldBackups-minDaysToKeep (15), cleanupFavorites, cleanupForests, cleanupViews, cleanupSynchronizers, cleanupStructureProperties, removeOldSyncAuditLogRecords, removeOldSyncAuditLogRecords-daysToKeep (30), reindexHistory, cleanupPerspectives, cleanupPerspectives-daysToKeep (30), reindexStructures, removeOldChangeHistory, removeOldChangeHistory-daysToKeep (30), removeOldChangeHistory-changesPerStructureToKeep (1000), removeOldEffectorProcesses, removeOldEffectorProcesses-daysToKeep (30), removeOldEffectorProcesses-waitingPreviewHoursToKeep (24), removeOldProcessStates, cleanupItemTracker; booleans as "true"/"false", numbers as decimal strings, e.g. {"backup":"true","removeOldBackups-minFilesToKeep":"5"}); 'maintenance.scheduled.nextRunTime' (epoch ms of next scheduled run) and 'maintenance.scheduled.nextRunTime.tz' (Java time zone id, e.g. 'Europe/Berlin', in which it was computed); 'maintenance.scheduled.currentProcessId' (id of the running maintenance process, AO_8BAD1B_PROCESS_STATE id); 'maintenance.manual.lastRunTime' (epoch ms); 'maintenance.successful' (boolean outcome of the last run, default true). Legacy key read during restore of old backups: 'view.defaultAssociatedViews_v2' (JSON in the same format as AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE_TO_VIEW.C_VIEW_SETTINGS, global default view settings from 2.x).

columns.C_KEY: Property key, non-blank, max 190 chars, primary key (see table summary for the keys and their value formats).
columns.C_VALUE: Property value as text (unlimited). Never empty in practice (empty means the row is deleted); a NULL value reads as absent.

AO_8BAD1B_FOLDER.summary: Stored folders: named grouping rows that users add to a structure. One row per folder. Created when a folder is added (or by restore with explicit ID), updated on rename, deleted when the folder is deleted (each change is announced as an item change of type '...:type-folder'). ID is the long item id of the folder's rows in AO_8BAD1B_ROW. (Text-only folders created by groupers are not stored here; they use string ids beginning with '/'.)

columns.ID: Auto-increment folder id (public, used directly as the '...:type-folder' long item id; no doubling).
columns.C_NAME: Folder name as shown in the structure, required, max 190 chars.
columns.C_OWNING_STRUCTURE: Id of the structure (AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE.ID) in which the folder was created and to which it belongs for permission purposes; NULL if not bound to a structure.

AO_8BAD1B_FAVORITES.summary: Users' favourite structures. One row per (user, structure) pair that is marked favourite; uniqueness is maintained by the application (marking deletes any existing pair rows and inserts one; unmarking deletes them). Rows are removed when the user's personal data is erased (all rows of that user) and by the maintenance option 'cleanupFavorites', which deletes rows whose user no longer exists or whose structure no longer exists. The number of rows per structure is the structure's popularity.

columns.ID: Auto-increment surrogate key; no meaning.
columns.C_USER_KEY: Jira user key (not user name) of the user, non-empty (default length 255).

AO_8BAD1B_STATISTICS.summary: One usage-statistics sample. Rows are append-only. Samples are buffered in memory and flushed by a periodic background job (default every 600 s, tunable via dark feature `structure.statisticsManager.pendingJobIntervalSeconds`; skipped while the plugin's database is locked), or written immediately when the browser posts statistics. A named statistic is either a 'total count' statistic (one row per flush with user null and the accumulated count in C_VALUE) or a 'unique user' statistic (one row per distinct user seen in the flush window, C_USERKEY set). No uniqueness constraint. Purge: a daily scheduled job (scheduled-job key `statistics.lastSentTime`, interval 86400000 ms, overridable via dark feature `almworks.statistics.dev.requestInterval`) deletes every row with C_TIMESTAMP older than now minus 40 days (3456000000 ms), then, if the admin opted in, sends an aggregated report off-site (see report notes). When a Jira user key changes (user anonymization), C_USERKEY values equal to the old key are rewritten to the new key. No foreign keys to other plugin tables.

columns.C_ID: Surrogate primary key, auto-increment 64-bit integer. No meaning.
columns.C_VALUE: Double. For a total-count statistic: the sum of increments collected during the flush window (usually an integer count such as 3.0; some sources add fractional or larger amounts). For a unique-user row it repeats the statistic's total if one was set, otherwise 0.0. The report sums C_VALUE over all rows with null user and divides by the number of days covered (average per day).
columns.C_TIMESTAMP: Epoch milliseconds of the sample: the time of the last event recorded into the buffer before the flush, or the client-supplied `timestamp` when the browser posts statistics via REST (so it may come from the client clock). Indexed; used for the 40-day purge and for date-range user counts.
columns.C_STAT: Statistic name, non-blank free-form dotted identifier, max 190 chars. Families: plain feature names (e.g. `perspectiveAccessCount`, `perspectiveShareCount`, `effectors.start.instance`, `effectors.effects.apply.success`, browser-reported UI action names such as `collapseAll`, `view.addColumn`); `userCount` and `activeUser` (unique-user statistics, recorded together with every browser report; `activeUser` only when the report includes one of a fixed set of interactive actions); `activeUser.<feature>` (unique users of a feature); distribution bins `<prefix>.<bin>` where <bin> is the smallest configured upper bound >= the value, written as a decimal integer, or `inf` if above all bounds (e.g. `effectors.previewSize.100`, `effectors.forestSize.inf`). Readers must accept unknown names.
columns.C_USERKEY: Jira user key (application user key, not user name) for unique-user statistics; null for total-count rows. A user without a key is stored as empty string. Rewritten on user-key change.

AO_8BAD1B_HISTORY_ENTRY.summary: One committed version step of a structure's stored (manual) forest: the header of a batch of forest changes made by one user or one synchronizer run in one transaction-like batch. Natural key is C_ID which packs (structure id, new forest version). Created whenever a batch of forest edits commits (also recreated verbatim when restoring a backup). Child rows: AO_8BAD1B_HISTORY_CHANGE (C_HID = this C_ID, the actual changes, in C_ID order), AO_8BAD1B_HISTORY_ISSUE and AO_8BAD1B_HISTORY_PROJECT (C_HID = this C_ID, search indexes). Purge: when a structure is deleted all its entries are removed (range [hid(s,0), hid(s+1,0)) in all four history tables); the maintenance task `removeOldChangeHistory` keeps, per structure, entries newer than `removeOldChangeHistory-daysToKeep` days (default 30) but at least the latest `removeOldChangeHistory-changesPerStructureToKeep` entries (default 1000) and deletes the older ones, again across all four tables by C_ID/C_HID range (0 for both settings means delete all history). On user-key change, C_USER_KEY is rewritten.

columns.C_ID: Packed history id (not auto-increment): (structureId << 32) | version, as a signed 64-bit integer, where structureId is AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE.ID (1..2^31-1) and version is the structure forest version produced by this entry (the value AO_8BAD1B_FOREST.C_VERSION took after the batch; >= 0). Example: structure 7, version 12 -> 7*4294967296+12 = 30064771084. All history of a structure is the C_ID range [s<<32, (s+1)<<32); ordering by C_ID orders by version.
columns.C_PREV_VERSION: Forest version of the structure immediately before this batch (int). Usually the previous entry's version, but versions can be skipped when changes are not recorded (so the gap between entries is meaningful: prev version != previous entry's version means unrecorded changes in between).
columns.C_TIMESTAMP: Epoch milliseconds when the entry was committed. Indexed; used for activity-stream date filters and day-based retention.
columns.C_USER_KEY: Jira user key of the user who made the change; null when no user (anonymous/system) — an empty key is normalized to null. Rewritten on user-key change/anonymization.
columns.C_SYNCHRONIZER: If the change was made by a synchronizer run: the AO_8BAD1B_SYNC_INSTANCE.ID of that installed synchronizer instance (only positive ids are recorded; one-time resyncs without an installed instance leave it null). Null for manual/user changes. The activity filter distinguishes 'any synchronizer' (not null) from 'none' (null).

AO_8BAD1B_HISTORY_CHANGE.summary: One elementary forest change inside a history entry. Several rows per entry, applied in ascending C_ID order (undo applies them in reverse). Consecutive compatible changes of the same kind are merged before writing (adjacent inserts at the same place, or moves/removals from the same spot become one row with a bigger forest). Created together with its AO_8BAD1B_HISTORY_ENTRY; deleted with it (see that table). Rows refer to structure rows by public row id, the same ids as in AO_8BAD1B_FOREST.C_FOREST (even, = AO_8BAD1B_ROW.ID * 2), in every row-id column; they may include rows whose ROW record no longer exists.

columns.C_ID: Auto-increment surrogate key; defines the order of changes within an entry.
columns.C_HID: AO_8BAD1B_HISTORY_ENTRY.C_ID of the owning entry (packed structure id and version). Indexed.
columns.C_OPERATION: Integer operation code: 1 = add (new rows inserted), 2 = copy (rows inserted as copies of existing rows), 3 = move (existing subtrees moved), 4 = remove (subtrees removed). Any other value is invalid and makes the entry unreadable.
columns.C_FOREST: JSON forest fragment affected by the change: `{"rows":[<rowId>,...],"depths":[<depth>,...]}` — two equally long arrays in depth-first order, row ids are public row ids (64-bit; even, = AO_8BAD1B_ROW.ID * 2, as in AO_8BAD1B_FOREST.C_FOREST), depths are 0-based relative to the fragment (roots have depth 0). For add/copy: the inserted rows; for move: the moved subtrees; for remove: the removed subtrees. Example: `{"rows":[101,102,103],"depths":[0,1,0]}` (101 with child 102, then 103). Never empty string.
columns.C_PATH_FROM: For move and remove: JSON array of row ids from the top level down to and including the former parent of the moved/removed rows (`[]` when they were at top level). Null for add and copy. Example `[55,60]`. Readers also accept a bare number (treated as one-element list) and treat JSON null elements as 0.
columns.C_AFTER_FROM: For move and remove: JSON array with the row id of the sibling that preceded the moved/removed rows in their old position, or `[]` if they were first under their parent. Null for add and copy. Example `[61]`.
columns.C_PATH_TO: For add, copy and move: JSON array of row ids from the top level down to and including the new parent (`[]` = inserted at top level). Null for remove.
columns.C_AFTER_TO: For add, copy and move: JSON array holding the row id after which the rows were placed, or `[]` if placed first under the parent. Null for remove.
columns.C_DIRECTION: Only for move: 1 if the moved rows ended up later in the flattened forest order than before (moved down), -1 if earlier (moved up). Null when 0/not applicable (add, copy, remove, or no positional change).
columns.C_ORIGINAL_ROWS: Only for copy: JSON array parallel to C_FOREST.rows giving, for each inserted row, the row id it was copied from, or 0 if the source row was not part of this structure's forest (or was a transient/generated row). Null for other operations. Example `[88,0,90]`.

AO_8BAD1B_HISTORY_ISSUE.summary: Search index row: Jira issue X was among the rows touched by history entry H (so the activity stream can be filtered by issue). One row per distinct (entry, issue) pair, written right after the entry and its changes, covering issues referenced by any row in any C_FOREST of that entry. Deleted together with the entry (by C_HID range).

columns.C_ISSUE_ID: Jira issue id (jiraissue.ID) of an issue item present in the changed forest fragment. Indexed.

AO_8BAD1B_HISTORY_PROJECT.summary: Search index row: an issue from Jira project P was among the rows touched by history entry H. One row per distinct (entry, project) pair, derived from the projects of the issues indexed in AO_8BAD1B_HISTORY_ISSUE for the same entry at the time of writing (not updated if issues later move). Deleted together with the entry (by C_HID range).

columns.C_PROJECT_ID: Jira project id (project.ID) of an issue touched by the entry. Indexed.

AO_8BAD1B_PERSPECTIVE.summary: A shared 'perspective': a saved snapshot of the structure page state (which structures/views/expansion are shown) that users share via link or e-mail; the link carries the id. Created when a licensed user with structure access shares the current page (REST POST perspective/share). Read anonymously-allowed by id; every successful read updates C_LAST_USED. Purge: maintenance task `cleanupPerspectives` deletes rows whose C_LAST_USED is older than `cleanupPerspectives-daysToKeep` days (default 30). Backup restore replaces the whole table (all rows deleted, then restored with their original ids and C_LAST_USED = restore time). No relations by column.

columns.C_ID: Perspective id, not auto-increment: a random integer in [1, 2147483647] (stored as 64-bit) chosen at creation; on a primary-key collision a new random id is tried, up to 10 attempts. Appears in shared URLs, so existing ids must be preserved.
columns.C_LAST_USED: Epoch milliseconds of creation or of the last retrieval by id (or of the restore). Indexed; drives the purge.
columns.C_SPEC: Non-empty client-defined JSON text describing the page state, stored verbatim as supplied by the browser. The server only interprets top-level keys `primary` and `secondary` (each an object describing a forest panel, which may contain `viewSpec`, a view specification in the same JSON shape the view REST API uses); on read, view specifications referencing saved columns are re-expanded from AO_8BAD1B_SAVED_COLUMN and the JSON is re-serialized, preserving all other keys. Example: `{"primary":{"forestSpec":{"structureId":12},"viewSpec":{"columns":[...]}},"secondary":null}`; `perspective-mail-sender` reads the structure from `primary.forestSpec.structureId`.

AO_8BAD1B_ISSUE_INDEX.summary: Reverse index 'which structures contain issue X': one row per (issue, structure) pair with the number of rows referencing that issue in the structure's stored forest (AO_8BAD1B_FOREST; generated rows are not counted). Natural key (C_ISSUE_ID, C_STRUCTURE_ID) is logically unique, not enforced: if duplicates are found, all but the first are deleted. Maintained incrementally on every forest change (count adjusted by the delta; row created when absent; row deleted when the count drops to 0). Rows of a structure are deleted when the structure is deleted. Full rebuild (maintenance task `reindexStructures`): all rows deleted, then one row inserted per issue per structure. Used to answer 'structures containing issue' (only rows with count > 0 count).

columns.ID: Auto-increment surrogate key.
columns.C_OCCURRENCES: Number (> 0) of rows in the structure's stored forest whose item is this issue (an issue can occur under several parents).

AO_8BAD1B_SYNC_INSTANCE.summary: One installed synchronizer: a synchronizer module bound to a structure with its parameters and owner. Created when a user installs a synchronizer on a structure (or by backup restore, which keeps the original ID). Updated when owner/parameters are edited or autosync is toggled. Deleted when the synchronizer is uninstalled, when its structure is deleted, when all synchronizers are uninstalled, and by maintenance task `cleanupSynchronizers` for instances whose structure no longer exists. Referenced by AO_8BAD1B_HISTORY_ENTRY.C_SYNCHRONIZER, AO_8BAD1B_SYNC_EVENT.C_SYNC_INSTANCE and AO_8BAD1B_SYNC_AUDIT_RECORD.C_SYNC_INSTANCE (no FK constraints; those rows may outlive the instance). One-time resyncs are not stored here. Note: the synchronizer UI is shown if dark feature `structure.feature.synchronizers.enabled` is on or if at least one row exists in this table.

columns.ID: Auto-increment synchronizer instance id (kept on restore). Positive.
columns.C_STRUCTURE_ID: AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE.ID of the structure being synchronized (int). Indexed.
columns.C_MODULE_KEY: Complete plugin module key of the synchronizer: `<pluginKey>:<moduleKey>`. Built-in values: `com.almworks.jira.structure:sync-filter` (saved filter/JQL), `com.almworks.jira.structure:sync-links` (issue links), `com.almworks.jira.structure:sync-gh` (Agile epics/rank), `com.almworks.jira.structure:sync-status-rollup` (status rollup), `com.almworks.jira.structure:sync-subtasks` (sub-tasks). Third-party plugins may register other keys; such rows must be preserved even if the module is absent.
columns.C_OWNER: Jira user key of the user on whose behalf the synchronizer runs (permissions are checked as this user).
columns.C_PARAMETERS: Synchronizer-specific serialized parameters, null when none (blank is normalized to null). For all built-in synchronizers it is a JSON object: sync-filter: `filterId` (long Jira saved-filter id, 0/absent when JQL used), `jql` (string), `add`, `remove` (booleans), `addRootIssue` (Jira issue id under which found issues are added; 0/absent = top level), `removeOnlyFromUnderAddRootIssue`, `recheckSubtreeWhenParentCanBeRemoved`, `moveFromUnderAnotherRoot` (booleans). sync-links: `linkTypeId` (long, Jira issue link type id), `childIsLinkSource` (bool), `parentFilterId`/`childFilterId` (long), `parentJql`/`childJql` (string), `expandChild`, `expandParent`, `useAllLinks` (bool), `primacy` (`links`|`structure`|`none`), `orphanAction` (`remove`|`moveUp`), `sourceOfTruth` (`jira`|`structure`). sync-gh: `sourceOfTruth` (`jira`|`structure`), `viewId` (long Agile board id; in project mode it is written as JSON null, and an absent or null `viewId` reads as 0), `projects` (array of Jira project ids; project mode only), `syncEpics`, `syncRank` (always written; in project mode true exactly when a rank field is chosen), `independentRanking`, `subtasks` (bool), `rankField` (rank custom field identifier string; written only in project mode and only when a rank field is chosen). sync-status-rollup: `applicableToAllProjects` (bool), `applicableProjects` (array of project ids), `applicableToAllTypes` (bool), `applicableTypes` (array of issue type id strings), `resolutionId` (string), `states` (array of `{"statusId":"<id>","allTransitionsAllowed":bool,"allowedTransitions":[{"workflowName":"...","actionId":<int>}]}`). sync-subtasks: `{"types":["<subtaskIssueTypeId>",...]}`. Example: `{"filterId":10100,"add":true,"remove":true,"removeOnlyFromUnderAddRootIssue":true}`.
columns.C_ENABLED: Autosync flag: true = runs incrementally on Jira/structure events; false = installed but only runs on explicit resync. Indexed.

AO_8BAD1B_SYNC_EVENT.summary: Cluster-wide queue of pending synchronizer events, used only on Jira Data Center (on a single server the queue is kept in memory and this table stays empty). Each row is one event: a Jira change relevant to synchronizers, a resync request, or an 'autosync enabled' marker. Rows are appended by any node; the node running synchronizers periodically reads all rows in ascending ID order and then deletes the rows it read (in batches of 100 ids; dark feature `structure.sync.deleteEventsBatchSize`). So rows are short-lived; no retention policy beyond consumption.

columns.ID: Auto-increment id; defines processing order.
columns.C_TYPE: Event type code: 1 = issue updated, 2 = issue link created, 3 = issue link deleted, 4 = epic link changed (Agile), 5 = rank changed (Agile), 6 = issue deleted, 126 = autosync enabled, 127 = resync request. Unknown codes fail an assertion when the events are drained: with assertions enabled (as the tests run) the drain throws AssertionError; with them disabled the row is skipped with a warning.
columns.C_DATA: JSON payload by type. Types 1, 4, 5, 6: a bare JSON number, the Jira issue id (e.g. `10234`). Types 2, 3: `{"linkTypeId":<long>,"sourceId":<issueId>,"destinationId":<issueId>}`. Type 126: two-element array `[<syncInstanceId>,<latestHistoryVersion>]` where the second is the latest AO_8BAD1B_HISTORY_ENTRY version, at the time autosync was enabled (>= 0), of the structure whose id equals the synchronizer instance id, not of the instance's own structure (as the original does), e.g. `[4,57]`. Type 127: object `{"instanceId":<long, 0 for one-time resync>,"structureId":<long>,"moduleKey":"<complete module key>","ownerKey":"<user key>","parameters":"<C_PARAMETERS string, empty if none>","processId":<AO_8BAD1B_PROCESS_STATE.ID or 0>,"autosyncEnabled":<bool>,"scheduledResync":<bool>}`. Never blank.
columns.C_TIMESTAMP: Epoch milliseconds when the event was recorded.
columns.C_SYNC_INSTANCE: AO_8BAD1B_SYNC_INSTANCE.ID of the synchronizer whose run caused this Jira change (so it can ignore its own changes), or null if the change was not made by a synchronizer.

AO_8BAD1B_SYNC_AUDIT_RECORD.summary: Synchronizer audit log. Records are grouped: a group header row (C_GROUP_ID = 0) describes one synchronizer action/run, followed by zero or more action rows (C_GROUP_ID = header's ID) listing the individual Jira-side changes the run made. Written in bulk by a background job every 30 s (dark feature `structure.sync.audit.pendingRecordsWriteInterval`; 0 disables auditing); groups with no actions are skipped unless dark feature `structure.sync.audit.writingEmptyGroups` is on (install/uninstall/enable events always have no actions, so they are written only in that case). Action rows are also the input for 'undo' of a synchronizer's changes, so their JSON must stay readable. Purge: maintenance task `removeOldSyncAuditLogRecords` deletes rows with C_TIMESTAMP older than `removeOldSyncAuditLogRecords-daysToKeep` days (default 30). Readers return at most 10000 rows per query (dark feature `structure.sync.audit.queryLimit`).

columns.ID: Auto-increment id. For header rows also the group id.
columns.C_SYNC_INSTANCE: AO_8BAD1B_SYNC_INSTANCE.ID the record belongs to; 0 for records not tied to an installed instance (global uninstall-all, one-time resync, undo). Set on both header and action rows. Indexed.
columns.C_SYNC_MODULE_KEY: Complete synchronizer module key (e.g. `com.almworks.jira.structure:sync-links`) on header rows; null on action rows and when unknown (empty is stored as null).
columns.C_STRUCTURE_ID: AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE.ID on header rows (0 when not structure-specific, e.g. uninstall-all or undo); null on action rows.
columns.C_TIMESTAMP: Epoch milliseconds when the group was recorded; header and its actions share the same value. Indexed.
columns.C_GROUP_ID: 0 for a group header row; otherwise the ID of the header row this action belongs to.
columns.C_DATA: JSON object. Header rows: description with key `action` = `install` | `installOffline` | `uninstall` | `uninstallAll` | `uninstallAllForStructure` | `setAutosyncEnabled` | `enableAfterResync` | `edit` | `sync` | `resync` | `undo`; management actions add `loggedInUserKey` (user key, may be empty) and (except uninstallAll*/undo) `parameters`: the synchronizer parameters as a JSON object (`{}` if none), except for `installOffline` and `uninstall`, where it is the stored parameter text as a JSON string; `installOffline` adds `autosyncEnabled` (bool), `setAutosyncEnabled` adds `enabled` (bool), `edit` (an update of the synchronizer's owner or parameters) adds `changedOwner` (bool), `changedParameters` (bool) and `ownerKey` (the owner's user key after the change); `sync`/`resync` headers add `ownerKey`, `parameters`, run-result keys (e.g. `result`: `success`|`failure`, `reason`, `exception` = `{message?, class, stackTrace, cause?}`), and for `sync` also `jiraEvents` (array of `{"timestamp":ms,"syncInstanceId":long,"type":"<change type name>","issues":[{"key":"ABC-1","id":10000}]}`) and `structureEvents` (array of `{"timestamp":ms,"syncInstanceId":long,"version":int}`). Action rows: synchronizer-specific objects, each with `type` and issue descriptors `{"key":"ABC-1","id":10000}`: links: `type` `createLink`|`removeLink` with `linkTypeId`, `source`, `destination`; Agile epics: `type` `changeEpic`|`removeFromEpic` with `issue`, `epic`, `oldEpic`, `epicLink` (link type id); Agile rank: `type` `updateRank` with `issue`, `newAfter` or `newBefore`, optional `oldBefore`/`oldAfter`, `rankField`; status rollup: `issue`, `oldStatus`, `newStatus` (`{"name","id"}`), `action` (`{"name","id"}` workflow transition). Any action may carry failure keys `result`=`failure`, `reason`, `exception`; failed actions are skipped by undo. Null allowed.

AO_8BAD1B_ORDERING.summary: Persisted manual order of sibling items for a 'manual sorting' automation (a sorter generator inserted into a structure that lets users drag rows to reorder generated content). One row per (sorter, parent path): the ordered list of items under that parent. Created/updated when a user reorders rows under such a sorter; deleted when the stored list becomes empty. Logically unique by C_KEY (not enforced; extra rows with the same key are deleted on update, first one wins on read). Not deleted when the sorter is removed (rows can be orphaned). Relation: C_SORTER_ID = AO_8BAD1B_GENERATOR.C_ID of the sorter; item tokens refer to AO_8BAD1B_ITEM_TYPE ids.

columns.ID: Auto-increment surrogate key.
columns.C_KEY: `<sorterId>.<path>`. <path> is `root` for top-level siblings, otherwise the comma-joined item tokens of all ancestors from the top of the forest down to the immediate parent of the ordered rows; when the ordered rows are group rows created by a grouper the path gets suffix `.gr`. Item identity token grammar (shared with other tables): a Jira issue is written as its decimal issue id alone (e.g. `10234`); any other item is `<typeId>/<longId>` (e.g. `3/57`) or, for items with a string id, `<typeId>//<urlEncodedStringId>` (e.g. `5//my%20item`), where <typeId> is the integer ID of the item type's row in AO_8BAD1B_ITEM_TYPE (created on demand) and the string id is percent-encoded like a URI component. Examples: `42.root`, `42.10001,3/7`, `42.10001.gr`. Readers fall back from a `.gr` key by dropping trailing group ancestors and finally to the same path without `.gr`. Indexed.
columns.C_ORDERING: Comma-separated item tokens (same grammar as in C_KEY) in the desired order, e.g. `10005,10003,3/12`; the single character `-` denotes an empty list. Items not listed are placed after the listed ones in their natural order; automation items are excluded.

AO_8BAD1B_PROCESS_STATE.summary: State of one long-running background process (e.g. maintenance run, backup/restore, effector application, resync) shown with a progress bar in the UI. Created PENDING when the process starts; updated with status, progress and display parameters as it runs; a cancel request sets C_CANCELLED. Deleted explicitly when the owner finishes with it, and by maintenance task `removeOldProcessStates`, which deletes rows whose C_TIMESTAMP is older than 30 days except those referenced by AO_8BAD1B_EFFECTOR_PROCESS.C_PROCESS_HANDLE_ID. The process id (this ID) is referenced from AO_8BAD1B_EFFECTOR_PROCESS.C_PROCESS_HANDLE_ID, resync requests (`processId` in AO_8BAD1B_SYNC_EVENT data) and the plugin's own property recording the currently running maintenance process.

columns.ID: Auto-increment process id (exposed to the UI/REST as the process handle id).
columns.C_TIMESTAMP: Epoch milliseconds of creation and, after that, of the last status change (progress updates do not touch it).
columns.C_STATUS: Status code: 0 = pending, 1 = running, 2 = finished. Any other value reads as finished.
columns.C_PARAMETERS: Display parameters as JSON or null: `{"name":<i18n text>,"buttons":[{"caption":<i18n text>,"url":"<relative or absolute url>"},...]}` where <i18n text> is `{"i18nKey":"<message key>","arguments":[...]}` (arguments are strings or numbers). Example: `{"name":{"i18nKey":"my.process.name","arguments":["7"]},"buttons":[{"caption":{"i18nKey":"my.button","arguments":[]},"url":"/some/page"}]}`. Unknown keys are ignored when reading.
columns.C_MANAGING_USER: Jira user key of the user who started/manages the process; null if none (empty normalized to null).
columns.C_ACTIVITY: Current activity description as an i18n text JSON `{"i18nKey":"...","arguments":[...]}`, or null before the first progress report.
columns.C_PERCENT_COMPLETE: Progress 0..100; -1 (set at creation) or null means unknown/indeterminate.
columns.C_CANCELLED: True once cancellation was requested; created false. Null reads as false.

AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE_PROPERTY.summary: Per-structure key/value property store (string values). One row per (structure, key); primary key is the composite string. Setting a blank/null value deletes the row. All rows of a structure are deleted when the structure is deleted; maintenance task `cleanupStructureProperties` deletes rows whose structure no longer exists. Copied when a structure is copied and included in backups. The store is exposed to other plugins via the public StructurePropertyService API, so arbitrary keys may exist and must be preserved. Known keys written by the plugin: `showDescription` (`true`/`false`: show the structure description on the structure page); `quick-transforms` (JSON array of quick transformation items for the structure toolbar, each `{"key":"<transform type key, or 'group'>","quick":{"id":"<unique id>","name":"...","color":"..."},"module":"<generator module key>","params":{...}}`, a group item having `"key":"group"` and `"transforms":[<items>]` instead of module/params; ids unique across the whole tree; default `[]`); `manualAdjustments.enable` (`true`/`false`: manual adjustments of generated content allowed in this structure); `generationTimeLimit` (decimal seconds, per-structure limit on forest generation time, overriding the global property of the same name; absent/0 = use global); `lastPolledMillis` (decimal epoch milliseconds of the last time the structure was opened/polled, written at most once per 2 hours per structure per node; shown as 'last used' in structure management).

columns.C_COMPOSITE_KEY: `<structureId>:<key>`, e.g. `12:showDescription`. <structureId> is AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE.ID in decimal (>= 0); <key> is at most 170 chars. Primary key.
columns.C_VALUE: The property value as a string (format depends on key, see summary). Non-blank in practice; null treated as absent.
columns.C_STRUCTURE_ID: AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE.ID, redundant with the key prefix; used for per-structure listing and deletion. Indexed.

AO_8BAD1B_S_ITEM_PROPERTY.summary: Per-structure, per-item key/value properties: values attached to an item (issue or other item) within a specific structure. The main use is structure notes: text notes shown in note columns. One row per (structure, item, property name); primary key is the composite string. Setting a blank value deletes the row. All rows of a structure are deleted when the structure is deleted (scan-and-delete by parsed key). Copied with structure copy, included in backup/restore and migration (where note property names are remapped to new note ids). Property names written by the plugin: `notes` (the default note) and `dc_note_<n>` where <n> is AO_8BAD1B_NOTE.ID (an additional named note); other names may be written via API and must be preserved.

columns.C_COMPOSITE_KEY: Pipe-separated: for items with a numeric id `<structureId>|<typeId>|<longItemId>|<propertyName>`; for items with a string id `<structureId>|<typeId>||<stringItemId>|<propertyName>` (empty field marks a string id; the string id is stored raw, not encoded, and may not contain `|`). <structureId> is AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE.ID (> 0); <typeId> is the integer ID of the item type in AO_8BAD1B_ITEM_TYPE (for issues the row with C_KEY `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-issue`), <longItemId> for issues is the Jira issue id; <propertyName> is non-blank, at most 160 chars. Examples: `12|1|10234|notes`, `12|4||abc|dc_note_3`. Rows whose key cannot be parsed are ignored.
columns.C_VALUE: Property value string, never blank (blank means delete). For notes: the note text exactly as entered by the user (multi-line plain text).

AO_8BAD1B_GENERIC_ITEM.summary: One row is one stored generic item: a user-created item that is not a Jira entity and is shown in structures. Two generic item types exist: memos (item type key `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-memo`) and planning tasks (`com.almworks.jira.structure:type-planning-task`); the type is told by C_TYPE_ID. The item identity used everywhere else (forests, rows, item properties) is (type key, ID), so ID is the item's numeric id and must be preserved. Rows are created when a user creates an item (auto-increment ID) and are also created with an explicit ID when a backup is restored (the ID from the backup is reused). Updated when the item is edited, or when the item is attached to a structure (C_OWNING_STRUCTURE set from null to that structure). If an already-owned item is placed into a different structure (e.g. when copying a structure), a NEW row is created as a copy owned by the target structure; the original is left alone. Deleted (hard delete by ID) when a user deletes the item; deletion does not remove its history rows (AO_8BAD1B_GENERIC_ITEM_HISTORY) and nothing deletes items when their owning structure is deleted. Each create and each user-visible update also appends a row to AO_8BAD1B_GENERIC_ITEM_HISTORY. Relations: C_TYPE_ID -> AO_8BAD1B_ITEM_TYPE.ID; C_OWNING_STRUCTURE -> AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE.ID; AO_8BAD1B_GENERIC_ITEM_HISTORY.C_LONG_ID + C_TYPE_ID -> this ID + C_TYPE_ID. A lookup by item identity must check that the row's type id matches the identity's type; a mismatch is treated as not found.

columns.ID: Item id (auto-increment integer, primary key). This is the numeric id in the item identity, e.g. memo 42 is (com.almworks.jira.structure:type-memo, 42). Explicit values are inserted on backup restore.
columns.C_NAME: Item display name, required. For a memo it is the memo text title; for a planning task it is the task summary (the `summary` field is stored here, not in the parameters). Plain text, up to 190 characters.
columns.C_OWNING_STRUCTURE: Id of the structure (AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE.ID) that owns the item, or null when the item is not owned by any structure. When non-null, the item is visible only to users who can view that structure; when null, it is visible to everyone who can see the referencing row.
columns.C_DESCRIPTION: Optional item description (the `description` field), unlimited text; for planning tasks it is Jira wiki-markup text as typed by the user. Null when absent.
columns.C_PARAMETERS: Item parameters as a JSON object (compact, null members omitted), or null when there are no parameters (an empty map is stored as null, never `{}`). Keys: `fields` (object, see below) for both types; memos additionally may have `color` (the colour value exactly as sent by the client, stored opaquely and returned as-is; also exposed as the memo attribute `color`) and `iconClass` (CSS class name string of the chosen icon). Unknown keys are preserved. Field-value map: the JSON object under key `fields` maps a Jira field id to a SERIALIZED STRING value (never a nested JSON value; the string itself may contain JSON). Field ids are Jira system field ids (`assignee`, `reporter`, `duedate`, `timeoriginalestimate`, `timeestimate`, `timespent`, `environment`, `priority`, `issuetype`, `project`, `labels`, `versions`, `fixVersions`, `components`) or custom field ids `customfield_<n>`; `summary` and `description` are never stored here (they live in the name/description columns). Value encodings by field kind: single-line and multi-line text: the raw text; single user (`assignee`, `reporter`, user picker): Jira user key, e.g. `JIRAUSER10100`; multi user: JSON array of user keys as strings, e.g. `["JIRAUSER10100","admin"]`; single group: group name; multi group: JSON array of group names; single select option: option id in decimal, e.g. `10200`; multi select: JSON array of option ids as strings, e.g. `["10200","10201"]`; date (`duedate`, date picker): ISO local date `yyyy-MM-dd`, e.g. `2026-10-28`; date-time picker: epoch milliseconds in decimal; durations (`timeoriginalestimate`, `timeestimate`, `timespent`): number of milliseconds in decimal, e.g. `7200000` for 2h; number field: a JSON number, e.g. `3.5` or `2.0`; project: project id written as a JSON floating number, e.g. `10000.0`; single version picker: version id in decimal; multi version (`versions`, `fixVersions`, multi version picker): JSON array of version ids as floating numbers, e.g. `[10001.0,10002.0]`; `components`: JSON array of component ids as strings, e.g. `["10100"]`; `labels` and label fields: JSON array of strings, e.g. `["backend","q4"]`; sprint field: the sprint id as a JSON string literal including the quotes, e.g. `"12"`; `issuetype` and `priority`: Jira constant id in decimal, e.g. `10001`. Null values are dropped from the map, and the `fields` key is removed when the map becomes empty. When neither estimate was set before and only one of `timeoriginalestimate`/`timeestimate` is now given, the other is filled with the same value. Example memo: `{"color":"blue","fields":{"assignee":"JIRAUSER10100","duedate":"2026-11-30"}}`. Example planning task: `{"fields":{"project":"10000.0","issuetype":"10001","timeoriginalestimate":"28800000","timeestimate":"28800000"}}`.
columns.C_TYPE_ID: Item type of this generic item, as AO_8BAD1B_ITEM_TYPE.ID of the type key (`com.almworks.jira.structure:type-memo` or `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-planning-task`; any item type registered as generic could appear). Integer, indexed.

AO_8BAD1B_ATOMIC_FLAG.summary: One row is one named cluster-wide flag holding a short string, updated with compare-and-set semantics (UPDATE ... WHERE C_KEY = ? AND C_VALUE = old, or C_VALUE IS NULL when the expected old value is null; success means exactly one row changed). Used on Jira Data Center to elect the single cluster node that performs a background duty. Known keys: `com.almworks.jira.structure.workNode.effector` (node that applies queued effector processes) and `com.almworks.jira.structure.workNode.autosync` (node that runs automatic synchronizers); the key grammar is `com.almworks.jira.structure.workNode.<duty>`. A row is inserted the first time a node tries to take the duty (insert races are resolved by the primary-key violation, the loser re-reads). The value is set to the taking node's id when the current holder is null or is not among the live cluster nodes; it is reset to null when the holding node shuts the duty down cleanly. Rows are never deleted. Not used on single-node (Server) installs.

columns.C_KEY: Flag name (primary key, up to 190 characters), e.g. `com.almworks.jira.structure.workNode.autosync`.
columns.C_VALUE: Current holder: the Jira cluster node id (as reported by Jira's cluster info, e.g. `node1`) of the node that owns the duty, or null when nobody owns it. Empty strings are normalised to null before writing.

AO_8BAD1B_MANUAL_ADJUSTMENTS.summary: One row per structure that has manual adjustments: the list of manual changes a user made to the generated (automation-produced) part of a structure's forest (adding items under generated rows, moving generated rows). Natural key = C_STRUCTURE_ID. Written with optimistic concurrency: the row is read, modified, and written back with UPDATE ... WHERE C_STRUCTURE_ID = ? AND C_VERSION = old version (up to 10 retries); the first write inserts with the new version (an insert conflict counts as a lost race). The total number of adjustments per structure is capped (default 2000; the change is rejected above it). The row is deleted when the structure is deleted or when a user clears all adjustments of the structure. Relations: C_STRUCTURE_ID -> AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE.ID; row ids inside the data are public row ids, as in AO_8BAD1B_FOREST.C_FOREST; item ids use AO_8BAD1B_ITEM_TYPE ids.

columns.C_VERSION: Change counter used for optimistic locking and as the id source of new adjustments. Starts at 0 meaning 'no row'; each applied change increments it by one, so the first stored version is >= 1. A newly added adjustment gets the new version number as its `id`.
columns.C_DATA: JSON array of adjustment objects (compact, null members omitted), or null/empty when there are none (an empty list is stored as null; a row with empty data is treated as no adjustments). Each object: `id` (int, the adjustment id, unique within the structure) and either an add form `{"id":..,"added":[rowSpec,..],"under":R,"after":R,"before":R}` or a move form `{"id":..,"moved":R,"under":R,"after":R,"before":R}`; a `removed` key is accepted on read but never written; unknown keys are ignored. `added` is a forest fragment, a list of strings `<rowId>:<depth>:<itemId>:<semantics>` in depth-first order (depth 0 = top of the fragment), where rowId is a public row id (as in AO_8BAD1B_FOREST.C_FOREST), itemId uses the compact item-id grammar below and semantics is the row's semantics code (long). R (a row identity) is one of: the number 0 (= the root / nothing, e.g. 'at top' or 'no after'), the number -1 (= missing/unknown row), a positive number (a plain row id), or a JSON array that is a path of row specs from the top, each spec being either a number (a row id) or a string `<itemId>:<semantics>` optionally followed by the letter `p` (`p` marks a persistent, non-generated row). Compact item-id grammar used here (shared with other columns of the plugin): an issue is written as its bare Jira issue id in decimal (e.g. `10234`); any other item is `<typeId>/<longId>` for items with a numeric id (e.g. `7/42`) or `<typeId>//<stringId>` for items with a string id (e.g. `5//jsmith`), where <typeId> is AO_8BAD1B_ITEM_TYPE.ID of the item type key (the registry assigns a new id on first use). Parsing regex: `(\d+)(?:/(?:(\d+)|/(.+)))?`; a lone number is always an issue. Example: `[{"id":3,"added":["901:0:10234:0","902:1:7/42:0"],"under":["12/5:0p","10500:0"],"after":0,"before":-1},{"id":4,"moved":["12/5:0p","10777:0"],"under":["12/5:0p"],"after":0,"before":0}]`. Unparseable data is logged and treated as empty.

AO_8BAD1B_EFFECTOR_INSTANCE.summary: One row is one configured effector instance: an effector (a module that computes changes to Jira data from a structure) together with its configuration, as inserted into a structure. Its row in a forest is the item (com.almworks.jira.structure:type-effector, ID). Created when a user adds an effector to a structure; updated when its configuration is edited; deleted (by ID) when explicitly deleted through the API. Not deleted automatically when the owning structure is deleted. On backup restore, rows are recreated with their original ID (module key and parameters only; the owning structure is left null on restore). Relations: C_OWNING_STRUCTURE -> AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE.ID; effector process parameters (AO_8BAD1B_EFFECTOR_PROCESS.C_PARAMETERS, key `effectorInstances`) embed copies of instances by id.

columns.ID: Effector instance id (auto-increment; explicit on restore); the numeric id of the effector item.
columns.C_MODULE_KEY: Complete plugin module key of the effector type, `<pluginKey>:<moduleKey>`. Bundled values: `com.almworks.jira.structure:effector-attribute-to-field`, `com.almworks.jira.structure:effector-status-rollup`, `com.almworks.jira.structure:effector-delay`, `com.almworks.jira.structure:effector-conversion`; third-party effectors use their own plugin key.
columns.C_PARAMETERS: Effector configuration as a JSON object whose keys are defined by the effector type (compact, null members omitted), or null when empty (an empty map is stored as null).
columns.C_OWNING_STRUCTURE: Structure (AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE.ID) the instance belongs to, or null if it is not attached to a structure.

AO_8BAD1B_EFFECTOR_PROCESS.summary: One row is one effector process: a run that first calculates a preview of effects (proposed changes to Jira issues/items) and, once confirmed, applies them. Three kinds, told apart by C_PARAMETERS: a run of the effector instances in a structure, a one-off run of an effector module over a forest spec, and an undo run that reverts selected effect records of an earlier process. Created by the user starting a run (status PENDING); all later state changes are conditional updates that check the current status (statement succeeds only if the row is still in the expected status). Lifecycle: PENDING -> CALCULATING (C_START_TIME set) -> CALCULATED (preview + C_FINISH_TIME set) or CALCULATION_FAILED (from PENDING/CALCULATING) or CALCULATION_STOPPED; CALCULATED (or directly after calculation when no confirmation is required) -> QUEUED (C_QUEUED set; preview kept) -> IN_PROGRESS (picked by the single applying node in order of C_QUEUED, null first; C_START_TIME reset to now and C_FINISH_TIME cleared) -> COMPLETED / COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS (C_FINISH_TIME set, C_EFFECTOR_PREVIEW cleared to null) or APPLY_STOPPED (cancel). Undo runs are created PENDING with the preview filled directly and immediately moved to QUEUED. At startup a node marks its own PENDING/CALCULATING rows (matching C_NODE_ID, or null node id on single-node) as CALCULATION_STOPPED; the applying job, on its first run after start, turns IN_PROGRESS and QUEUED into APPLY_INTERRUPTED, and on later runs returns IN_PROGRESS rows to QUEUED; an APPLY_INTERRUPTED process can be resumed (-> QUEUED, C_ACKNOWLEDGED reset to false). The user acknowledges a finished process (COMPLETED, COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS, APPLY_INTERRUPTED, APPLY_STOPPED) which sets C_ACKNOWLEDGED; unacknowledged processes of a user are listed as 'running' for that user, newest C_CREATED first. Purge: a maintenance task (key `removeOldEffectorProcesses`) deletes processes in COMPLETED, COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS, APPLY_INTERRUPTED or APPLY_STOPPED whose C_FINISH_TIME is older than N days (default 30, setting `removeOldEffectorProcesses-daysToKeep`) together with their AO_8BAD1B_EFFECTOR_RECORD rows, and processes in PENDING, CALCULATING, CALCULATED, CALCULATION_STOPPED or CALCULATION_FAILED whose C_CREATED is older than M hours (default 24, setting `removeOldEffectorProcesses-waitingPreviewHoursToKeep`); a user may also delete a CALCULATED/CALCULATION_STOPPED/CALCULATION_FAILED process. Each delete also deletes the linked process handle row (AO_8BAD1B_PROCESS_STATE). User anonymisation rewrites C_USER_KEY from the old key to the new one. Relations: C_PROCESS_HANDLE_ID -> AO_8BAD1B_PROCESS_STATE.ID; AO_8BAD1B_EFFECTOR_RECORD.C_PROCESS_ID -> ID; parameters refer to AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE.ID, AO_8BAD1B_EFFECTOR_INSTANCE.ID and to other processes.

columns.ID: Process id (auto-increment integer).
columns.C_PARAMETERS: Run parameters as a JSON object (compact, null members omitted, unknown keys ignored on read). Keys: `structureId` (long, structure the run works on; present for instance runs, copied into undo runs); `effectorInstances` (array of effector instance snapshots, each `{"id":<instance id>,"moduleKey":"<complete module key>","owningStructure":<structure id, omitted if null>,"parameters":{..effector config..}}`, instance runs only); `oneOffEffectorModuleKey` (string, complete effector module key, one-off runs); `oneOffParams` (object, effector configuration for a one-off run); `oneOffForestSpec` (object, the forest the one-off run covers, in the REST forest-spec format of com.almworks.jira.structure.api.rest.RestForestSpec: keys `structureId`, `version`, `sQuery` {`query`,`type`}, `type`, `transforms` [{`module`,`key`,`params`}], `title`; copied into undo runs); `revertedProcessId` (long, the process being undone; undo runs only). Example: `{"structureId":128,"effectorInstances":[{"id":7,"moduleKey":"com.almworks.jira.structure:effector-status-rollup","owningStructure":128,"parameters":{"x":1}}]}`.
columns.C_EFFECTOR_PREVIEW: Calculated preview as a JSON object `{"previewEffects":[effect,..],"errors":[text,..]}` (either key may be absent), or null (before calculation, and after the process completes or is stopped, the preview is cleared). An effect is `{"moduleKey":"<complete effect-provider module key>","parameters":{..}}`, e.g. `{"moduleKey":"com.almworks.jira.structure:assignee-effect-provider","parameters":{"issue":10234,"assignee":"JIRAUSER10100"}}`; effect-provider keys are `com.almworks.jira.structure:<key>` with key one of the bundled providers (assignee-, priority-, description-, environment-, resolution-, summary-, due-date-, reporter-, status-, cascade-custom-field-, project-picker-custom-field-, script-runner-single-issue-picker-, single-select-custom-field-, portfolio-team-custom-field-, single-user-custom-field-, single-group-custom-field-, single-version-custom-field-, text-custom-field-, number-custom-field-, date-custom-field-, date-time-custom-field-, labels-, multi-versions-custom-field-, affects-versions-, fix-versions-, components-, multi-select-custom-field-, multi-user-custom-field-, multi-group-custom-field-, multi-labels-custom-field-, insight-object-custom-field-, warning-, delay-, original-estimate-, remaining-estimate-, sprint-, add-comment-, delete-comment-, memo-field-, conversion- each followed by `effect-provider`) or third-party ones; parameter keys are provider-specific (common ones: `issue` issue id, `customField` field id, `value`, `from`, `to`, `add`/`remove` lists, `conflicts`, `memo` item id string with `field` and `value` for memo fields; the public type com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect.CoreEffects documents the core ones). A text in `errors` is `{"i18nKey":"<message key>","arguments":[..]}`.
columns.C_STATUS: Process status, the enum constant name as text, one of: `PENDING` (created, preview not yet calculated), `CALCULATING` (preview calculation running), `CALCULATED` (preview ready, waiting for user confirmation), `CALCULATION_FAILED` (preview failed; errors are in C_EFFECTOR_PREVIEW), `CALCULATION_STOPPED` (preview calculation cancelled by the user or abandoned because the node restarted), `QUEUED` (confirmed, waiting to be applied), `IN_PROGRESS` (effects being applied), `COMPLETED` (all effects applied), `COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS` (applied, some effects failed), `APPLY_INTERRUPTED` (application stopped by a restart and not resumed), `APPLY_STOPPED` (application cancelled by the user).
columns.C_USER_KEY: Jira user key of the user who started the process (rewritten on user anonymisation).
columns.C_PROCESS_HANDLE_ID: Id of the process handle row in AO_8BAD1B_PROCESS_STATE (progress tracking of this process); that row is deleted with the process.
columns.C_START_TIME: Epoch ms when calculation started (set on PENDING -> CALCULATING) and overwritten with the time application started (QUEUED -> IN_PROGRESS); null before.
columns.C_FINISH_TIME: Epoch ms when the latest phase ended (calculation finished/failed/stopped, or application completed/stopped/aborted by restart cleanup); set to null when a queued process is picked for applying. Used for purging finished processes.
columns.C_QUEUED: Epoch ms when the process was put into the applying queue (status QUEUED); the queue is served in ascending order of this value (rows with null first). Null if never queued.
columns.C_CREATED: Epoch ms when the process row was created. Used to list newest first and to purge stale previews.
columns.C_NODE_ID: Jira cluster node id of the node that created the process (used to abandon its calculations when that node restarts); null on a non-clustered (single-node) install.
columns.C_ACKNOWLEDGED: False on creation (and on resume); set true when the user acknowledges a finished process (only allowed in COMPLETED, COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS, APPLY_INTERRUPTED, APPLY_STOPPED).

AO_8BAD1B_EFFECTOR_RECORD.summary: One row is the outcome of applying one effect of an effector process (one entry of the process preview): a message, an error flag, the effect that would undo it, and the items it touched. Rows are appended while a process is IN_PROGRESS, one per effect attempted; never updated. Deleted together with the process by the effector-process purge (see AO_8BAD1B_EFFECTOR_PROCESS). Undo runs read the records of the reverted process and use their C_UNDO_EFFECT values (optionally only selected C_PREVIEW_INDEX values) as their preview. Relations: C_PROCESS_ID -> AO_8BAD1B_EFFECTOR_PROCESS.ID.

columns.ID: Record id (auto-increment integer).
columns.C_PROCESS_ID: Id of the effector process (AO_8BAD1B_EFFECTOR_PROCESS.ID) this record belongs to. Indexed.
columns.C_EFFECT_MESSAGE: Human-readable result message as JSON. Plain form: `{"i18nKey":"<message key>","arguments":[..]}`. Form with user references: `{"i18nKey":..,"arguments":[..],"argumentsWithUserKeys":[..]}`, where `arguments` holds the arguments resolved to display text at write time and `argumentsWithUserKeys` holds the same arguments as strings in which each user is written as `${<user key>}` (e.g. `"${JIRAUSER10100}"`); readers re-resolve each `${...}` to the user's current display name (or an 'unknown user' text) when the key `argumentsWithUserKeys` is present.
columns.C_ERROR: True if applying this effect failed (the message then describes the error), false if it succeeded.
columns.C_UNDO_EFFECT: The effect that reverts this one, as JSON `{"moduleKey":"<complete effect-provider module key>","parameters":{..}}` (same effect format as in the process preview); an empty string (or null) when no undo is possible.
columns.C_AFFECTED_ITEMS: Items changed by the effect, as a JSON array of strings in the compact item-id grammar, or null when none. Compact item-id grammar used here (shared with other columns of the plugin): an issue is written as its bare Jira issue id in decimal (e.g. `10234`); any other item is `<typeId>/<longId>` for items with a numeric id (e.g. `7/42`) or `<typeId>//<stringId>` for items with a string id (e.g. `5//jsmith`), where <typeId> is AO_8BAD1B_ITEM_TYPE.ID of the item type key (the registry assigns a new id on first use). Parsing regex: `(\d+)(?:/(?:(\d+)|/(.+)))?`; a lone number is always an issue. Example: `["10234","9/42"]`.
columns.C_TIMESTAMP: Epoch ms when the effect was applied.
columns.C_PREVIEW_INDEX: Zero-based index of the effect within the process preview's `previewEffects` array that this record is the outcome of.

AO_8BAD1B_MIGRATION_CONFIG.summary: One row is one named cloud-migration configuration: which structures (and which optional add-on data) to send when Atlassian's Jira Cloud Migration Assistant runs an app-data migration whose migration plan has the same name. Natural key = C_NAME (unique). Created/edited/deleted by an administrator on the migration configurations admin page (each save sets C_EDITED_AT/C_EDITED_BY and saves status DRAFT or READY, with C_RUN_AT reset to null). During a cloud migration the plugin looks up the row whose C_NAME equals the migration plan name; if found and its status is not runnable (DRAFT or RUNNING) the app data migration is skipped; otherwise status goes READY -> RUNNING -> DONE or FAILED, and C_RUN_AT is set when it ends (other columns are kept). If no row matches, all structures are migrated. Relations: C_STRUCTURE_IDS lists AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE.ID values.

columns.ID: Configuration id (auto-increment integer).
columns.C_NAME: Configuration name, unique; must match the Jira Cloud Migration Assistant migration plan name to be used. Up to 190 characters.
columns.C_STATUS: Status as text, one of `DRAFT` (saved but not published; not runnable), `READY` (published, runnable), `RUNNING` (a migration is in progress; not runnable), `DONE` (last run succeeded; runnable again), `FAILED` (last run failed; runnable again).
columns.C_STRUCTURE_IDS: Structures to migrate, as a JSON array of structure ids (numbers), e.g. `[12,57,130]`; `[]` means none selected, which the migration treats as 'migrate all structures'. A row holding the empty string cannot be read back: reading it fails (as the original does). Never null (empty string written instead of null). A single bare number is also accepted on read.
columns.C_EXTENSION_KEYS: Optional add-on data to include, as a JSON array of Jira app (plugin) keys of apps that contribute structure backup data, e.g. `["com.almworks.structure.gantt"]`; null when the set is empty.
columns.C_RUN_AT: Epoch ms when the last migration using this configuration finished (DONE or FAILED); null when it has not run since the last save or is running.
columns.C_EDITED_AT: Epoch ms of the last create/edit by an administrator.
